feedback: D1 is the strongest part of this submission. You catalogued all ten of the real findings plus a defensible enumeration extra, and every core finding carries a quoted source line or a capture timestamp, for example SQLi at 01 L40 with capture 02:15:31 admin' OR '1'='1, the hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 at L15, alg:none tied to 03 Token 2, and XXE tied to 04-import-xxe.xml. Your CWE numbers are right throughout; the only slip is OWASP category drift, you filed the JWT issues under A02 and A04 where alg:none is A07 and open redirect is A01, but the evidence and CWE carry the proof so I did not punish that hard. The decoy is handled correctly: you named the hash_equals construct, proved it constant-time at the mechanism level, and crucially kept alg:none on the live vulnerability list rather than mislabelling it the decoy, which is exactly right. D2 reconstructs the chain in order with timestamps that reconcile to the pack, from enumeration at 02:14:55 through SQLi 02:15:31, harvest 02:16:04, XSS 02:18:47, redirect 02:21:13, file read 02:24:02, and exfil, and your F1 vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at 9.1 is spot on. Two things cost you on D2: your per-hop PoC is thinner than the chain table, the verbatim payloads live mostly in D1 rather than reconciled to each hop, and your F3/F4 CVSS uses A:H and S:U to reach 9.8 when the bypass does not hit availability and, more importantly, the forged super_admin token reaches the shared /api/v1/internal service, which is a scope change S:C you missed, and none of your vectors carry a justifying sentence. D3 reads like a report Bayo can act on: the executive summary lands on the 312 customers and naira headline, the threat model names systems and the Griot adversary, the decoy is restated correctly, and your remediation section is genuinely ranked by risk reduction per hour of effort rather than raw CVSS, which is the right axis, though the Risk/Hour numbers are internally inconsistent with the ranking. Where D3 loses marks is the detection stopgaps: you gave a WAF regex and a SIEM alpha:none query but neither carries a false-positive rate, which the brief asked for explicitly. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice, cites ISC2 Canon I and II load-bearing, and anchors to the 312 records, but you cited NDPA Section 31 for the 72-hour duty when the breach notification sections are 40 (notify the NDPC within 72 hours) and 41 (notify data subjects on high risk); naming the wrong section cost most of that row. I looked for a way to round the CVSS and detection rows higher and the evidence did not support it, the vectors are bare and the FP rates are simply absent. The single most important fix: when you score CVSS, write one justifying sentence per vector and trace scope, the super_admin token crossing into /api/v1/internal makes the critical path S:C, not S:U.
